questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A high academic level and a city with a tangible presence of philosophical thinking embedded in the Parisian culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult – Sorbonne Université is not very digitalized compared to UCPH and all the bureaucratic stuff takes a lot of time and energi.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is a Erasmus orientation meeting and a meeting with the Erasmus coordinator of the exchange students on philosophy. Otherwise you have to find all the information on your self. I discovered very late in the semestre that there are WhatsApp-groups for all the different philosophy masters – it is in these groups that all the important messages about exams, for example, are shared.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in Fondation Danoise and loved it! I would really recommend applying for a spot in Fondation Danoise (if you are not accepted, you might get a spot in one of the other houses in Cité Universitaire).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are not a lot of opportunities for social engagement on campus (or maybe I just didn't find them), so I would recommend Fondation Danoise for the possibility of getting a social network in an easy way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was difficult to get any information beforehand but when you arrive it becomes quite simple because everything is handled face-to-face.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much I would say – I recommend asking some of the "regular" students for information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: That is also very complicated – first of all to find out which courses are available (through the brochures available online once a year) then we had to registrer through a google sheets link (shared during the orientation with our Erasmus coordinator). I changed some courses during the first few weeks and were able to change it in the google sheets pretty easily because they hadn't confirmed and registrated my choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different courses : they differ very much in the level and the type of exam.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was high but not too high – the difficult part was the language.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar to philosophy – mostly professors doing lectures without student participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Les penseurs de l'émancipation face à la violence
Éthique et herméneutique
Valeurs de l'art I
Approches de l'œuvre d'art chez Merleau-Ponty : forme et expression
Séminaire Victor Basch

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked all of them. The first two courses were on the master "Philosophie politique et éthique" and they were easier, especially because there were no mid-term-exams and the final evaluation was easier, than on the last three courses on the master "Esthétique et philosophie de l'art".

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You spend a lot of money on restaurants, museums (which are cheaper than in DK), concerts, clubs etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books are cheap!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use any of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To live in the Cité Universitaire!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spend time in all the different areas of Paris, you never run out of museums that you haven't seen, for example.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The language makes it difficult unless you speak french fluently.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are not very open, so I gave up on it – but there are also a lot of interesting exchange students from all over europe that are very open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Again the language!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of history and art to discover.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be ready for a big challenge regarding the language (if you are not fluent), take us of being in on the cultural hearts of europa and remember to enjoy it with someone (it is easy to be alone in Paris but much more fun to share with new friends or visitors from home).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You find the available courses in the brochures online – they publish them shortly before the beginning of a school year. And remember to get someone to add you to the WhatsApp-groups.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to study in french and getting a lot of new friends (especially by living in Fondation Danoise)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
